cards.text: The LORD has sent Jeremiah, His prophet, down to the palace of Judah's king with a message (Jeremiah 22:1). Now the message gets personal, one royal at a time. And it opens with a twist: don't weep for the one who's dead, and don't mourn his loss.

cards.question: Don't weep for the one who's dead, Jeremiah says. So who should the people weep bitterly for instead?

cards.text: The LORD names him: Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who took his father's place and is now gone from here. And the LORD says he's never coming back, not 'back next week,' not 'back for the holidays,' NEVER.

cards.question: Shallum won't come home to Judah. The LORD says he will ___ in the place where he was exiled.

cards.text: Then the LORD calls out a woe on the man who builds his palace by unrighteousness and his upper rooms without justice. Friend, when the LORD's review of your house starts with 'Woe,' it is NOT getting five stars.

cards.question: This palace builder needs workers. How does he treat the countrymen doing the work?

answers.text: He makes them serve without pay
He works them through the Sabbath
He forces them to fight his wars

cards.text: He says, "I will build myself a great palace, with spacious upper rooms." Windows, cedar panels, vermilion paint, the whole showroom, and then the LORD asks him, "Does it make you a king to excel in cedar?"

cards.question: The LORD asks the palace builder if excelling in cedar makes him a king. The point of that question is that a fancy palace doesn't make a real king.

cards.text: Then the LORD points to the man's father: he had food and drink, he administered justice and righteousness, and so it went well with him. No cedar mentioned, friend, not one plank.

cards.question: The palace builder's father did justice and righteousness. He took up the cause of the ___ and ___.
The LORD says taking up the cause of the poor and needy is what it means to know Him.
Now back to the son with the cedar palace. What does the LORD say his eyes and heart are set on?

cards.text: Dishonest gain, shedding innocent blood, extortion and oppression, that's the whole list. So the LORD names him, Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, yes, ANOTHER son of Josiah, and tells what happens when he dies.

cards.question: When Jehoiakim dies, the people will mourn for him, crying "Alas, my master!"

cards.text: No mourning for Jehoiakim. Instead, the LORD says he will be buried like a donkey.

cards.question: Jehoiakim will be buried like a donkey. What does the LORD say happens to his body?

answers.text: Dragged away and thrown outside the gates
Laid to rest in the tomb of his fathers
Carried up to the city of David

cards.text: Dragged and thrown out, friend. I got slid to the back of a junk drawer once and called it the worst day of my life, but nobody DRAGGED me.
Now the message calls out: go up to Lebanon and cry out, raise your voice in Bashan, cry out from Abarim. Three places to shout from, friend, that's not a cry, that's a TOUR.

cards.question: Cry out from Lebanon, from Bashan and from Abarim. Why all the crying?

answers.text: All your lovers have been crushed
All your fields have been burned
All your gates have been shut

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "I warned you when you were secure. You said, ‘I will not listen.’" That's putting tape over the check engine light because the car still runs fine.

cards.question: The LORD says not obeying His voice is something new for them.

cards.text: Still talking to the one told to cry out, the LORD says the wind will drive away all your shepherds. WHOOSH, gone, like my parchment paper every time a baker leaves the bakery door open.

cards.question: The wind drives away the shepherds. And the LORD says the lovers will go into ___.

cards.text: Then comes shame and humiliation, because of all the wickedness. And to the one nestled in the cedars of Lebanon, all cozy, the LORD says pangs of anguish are coming, and how you will groan.

cards.question: Pangs of anguish are coming to the one nestled in the cedars. What does the LORD compare that agony to?

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to Coniah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah. That's Josiah's grandson, friend, this message is going through the family like a group chat.
Then the LORD swears by His own life, "As surely as I live," and brings up a signet ring on His right hand. Friend, when He opens like THAT, you sit down.

cards.question: The LORD says even if Coniah were a signet ring on His right hand, He would keep him close.

cards.text: In fact, the LORD says He'll hand Coniah over to the ones he dreads, the ones who want to take his life. Not exactly a welcome committee.

cards.question: Coniah is handed over to the ones he dreads. Who are they?

cards.text: So Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, gets Coniah. And the LORD says He'll hurl Coniah and the mother who gave him birth into another land, where neither of them was born.

cards.question: Coniah and his mother end up in a land where neither of them was born. The LORD says there they both will ___.

cards.text: Coniah will never return to the land he longs for. Then comes a question: is this man Coniah something despised and broken that no one wants, and why are he and his descendants hurled out into a land they do not know?

cards.question: The question pictures Coniah as something despised and broken that no one wants. What is it?

cards.text: Then it's "O land, land, land, hear the word of the LORD!" Friend, when the whole LAND gets called three times, everybody puts the phone down.

cards.question: The LORD's last word on Coniah. True or false: none of his descendants will prosper to sit on the throne of David or rule again in Judah.
No descendant of Coniah on David's throne. So how does the LORD say to enroll Coniah, a man who will not prosper in his lifetime?
